newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco Sudbury union says talks going poorly.
newsitem.headline: Inco Sudbury union says talks going poorly.

text.p: The union representing 4,700 Inco Ltd workers in Ontario said on Wednesday contract talks are going poorly ahead of a weekend strike deadline.
Negotiators for the United Steeworkers of America and Inco are trying to hammer out a new agreement before the current contract expires at midnight on Saturday, May 31.
"It looks like things are going poorly," Gary Patterson, vice-president of Steelworkers' local 6500, said in a telephone interview.

Patterson said monetary issues had not yet been put on the negotiating table. He added that unless a tentative agreement is reached by Thursday, the union may not have enough time to put it to a vote before the Saturday strike deadline.
"If we don't have an offer by tommorrow morning then we could still have a strike," Patterson said. He said the union would not extend the deadline.
On Monday, the Steelworkers said they had requested the assistance of a provincial mediator after talks reached an impasse over the weekend.
Workers at Inco's Ontario operations have voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders a mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.
